claims.claim: Grinblat and Bucklew say they deliberately let players employ apophenia, the human tendency to perceive patterns, rather than prescribing a narrative morphology.
claims.source: Jason Grinblat and C. Brian Bucklew, 'Subverting Historical Cause & Effect: Generation of Mythic Biographies in Caves of Qud', FDG'17, Aug 2017
claims.quote: apophenia, the human tendency to perceive patterns

claims.claim: Grinblat and Bucklew say they aimed for evocative biographical narratives rather than meticulously detailed ones.
claims.source: Jason Grinblat and C. Brian Bucklew, 'Subverting Historical Cause & Effect: Generation of Mythic Biographies in Caves of Qud', FDG'17, Aug 2017

claims.claim: Grinblat and Bucklew say they did not aim to explicitly simulate historical logic, and instead generated history in order to simulate historical accounts.
claims.source: Jason Grinblat and C. Brian Bucklew, 'Subverting Historical Cause & Effect: Generation of Mythic Biographies in Caves of Qud', FDG'17, Aug 2017
claims.quote: we didn't aim to explicitly simulate historical logic

claims.claim: Grinblat and Bucklew say places named in a sultan's generated life are instantiated as historic sites during world generation.
claims.source: Jason Grinblat and C. Brian Bucklew, 'Subverting Historical Cause & Effect: Generation of Mythic Biographies in Caves of Qud', FDG'17, Aug 2017
claims.quote: instantiated as historic sites during world generation
claims.page: section 4.6, Impact on the Generated World

claims.claim: Grinblat and Bucklew report that gospels appear in 14 of the 150 most popular screenshots uploaded to the Caves of Qud Steam community page over six months.
claims.source: Jason Grinblat and C. Brian Bucklew, 'Subverting Historical Cause & Effect: Generation of Mythic Biographies in Caves of Qud', FDG'17, Aug 2017
claims.quote: gospels are featured in 14 of the 150 most popular screenshots

claims.feature: other: pool size as a variety input
claims.claim: Grinblat and Bucklew say output variety would be improved by expanding the set of domains, then numbering ten, and the suite of historical events, then numbering nineteen.
claims.source: Jason Grinblat and C. Brian Bucklew, 'Subverting Historical Cause & Effect: Generation of Mythic Biographies in Caves of Qud', FDG'17, Aug 2017
claims.quote: the set of domains (currently numbering ten)

claims.claim: Grinblat and Bucklew propose as future work that one event generate multiple, conflicting gospels from different perspectives.
claims.source: Jason Grinblat and C. Brian Bucklew, 'Subverting Historical Cause & Effect: Generation of Mythic Biographies in Caves of Qud', FDG'17, Aug 2017

claims.claim: Grinblat and Bucklew say Caves of Qud relies on a corpus of over 40,000 words to establish its voice, and that the replacement grammar let them codify that diction and repackage it procedurally.
claims.source: Jason Grinblat and C. Brian Bucklew, 'Subverting Historical Cause & Effect: Generation of Mythic Biographies in Caves of Qud', FDG'17, Aug 2017

claims.feature: other: templates become visible with repetition
claims.claim: Jonathan Lessard, quoted in Ryan's dissertation, argues that readers will soon see through authored story patterns used to retrieve stories from a simulation.
claims.source: James Ryan, 'Curating Simulated Storyworlds', PhD dissertation, UC Santa Cruz, Dec 2018
claims.quote: readers will soon see through them

claims.claim: Lessard, quoted in Ryan, characterises the repeated template as the same story with a different name substituted.
claims.source: James Ryan, 'Curating Simulated Storyworlds', PhD dissertation, UC Santa Cruz, Dec 2018
claims.quote: except with Bob instead of John

claims.feature: other: sifting only finds what it was told to find
claims.claim: Ryan concedes that a system sifting a simulated history can only excavate material that matches the patterns it was given.
claims.source: James Ryan, 'Curating Simulated Storyworlds', PhD dissertation, UC Santa Cruz, Dec 2018
claims.quote: the computer can only excavate material that matches those particular patterns

claims.claim: Ryan names boringness as a fundamental pitfall of emergent narrative, saying some simulations are too boring to yield stories.
claims.source: James Ryan, 'Curating Simulated Storyworlds', PhD dissertation, UC Santa Cruz, Dec 2018

claims.claim: Ryan quotes Mike Cook's pronouncement that the aesthetics of big numbers is dead, made in the context of boredom with No Man's Sky.
claims.source: James Ryan, 'Curating Simulated Storyworlds', PhD dissertation, UC Santa Cruz, Dec 2018
claims.quote: the aesthetics of big numbers is dead

claims.claim: Gillian Smith, quoted by Douglas Heaven in New Scientist and relayed by Ryan, says size alone is not enough to sustain interest in a generated world.
claims.source: James Ryan, 'Curating Simulated Storyworlds', PhD dissertation, UC Santa Cruz, Dec 2018
claims.quote: size alone is not enough to sustain interest

claims.claim: Ryan says each Talk of the Town emergent scenario stands against the monotony of everyday existence that constitutes the far majority of a town's history.
claims.source: James Ryan, 'Curating Simulated Storyworlds', PhD dissertation, UC Santa Cruz, Dec 2018
claims.quote: the monotony of everyday existence that constitutes the far majority
claims.page: Chapter 10, on aesthetics of a larger context
